recipes.name: Maryland crab cakes
recipes.description: Maryland crab cakes is a Maryland-style dish featuring cooked crab meat, seared in a hot pan, with 1 egg, 50 g breadcrumbs. Tip: Pat seafood dry before searing to encourage browning.
instructions: Prepare the seafood and measure the seasonings. If the recipe includes a coating, combine it in a shallow dish and coat evenly.
Heat a heavy pan with the listed oil over medium heat. Cook in batches so the pan stays hot and the seafood browns rather than steams.
Turn carefully and cook seafood to 63 C; shellfish flesh should be opaque. Drain fried pieces on a rack or paper.
Finish with the listed citrus or herbs and serve promptly.
recipes.sides: Serve with lemon, slaw and tartar sauce.
recipes.substitutions: Use cooked white fish flakes.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked leftovers in a covered shallow container within 2 hours and use within 3 days; reheat once until steaming. Do not save raw marinade that touched meat or seafood.
recipes.safety: Keep raw seafood chilled and separate from ready-to-eat foods. Cook fish to 63 C; shrimp, scallops, crab and lobster should be firm and opaque. Discard clams and mussels that do not open. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Use clean, uncracked eggs and cook the centre through.

recipes.name: Southern fried catfish
recipes.description: Southern fried catfish is a Southern United States-style dish featuring catfish fillets, about 700 g, lightly coated and fried until crisp, with 200 ml buttermilk, 120 g cornmeal. Tip: Fry in small batches so the oil temperature does not drop.
instructions: Pat the seafood dry and prepare the flour or crumb coating. Heat oil in a heavy pan to 175 C, using a thermometer and leaving plenty of headroom.
Fry in small batches until crisp and golden, turning once. Keep uncooked batches chilled while the oil heats.
Check thick pieces reach 63 C; drain on a rack and let the oil return to temperature between batches.
Serve hot with the listed sauce and lemon. Keep water away from hot oil.

instructions: Soften the onion and aromatics in a saucepan with the listed oil. Add the vegetables and measured stock and bring to a simmer.
Cook until the vegetables are tender, then add fish or shellfish according to thickness, starting with the firmest pieces.
Simmer gently until fish reaches 63 C and shellfish is firm and opaque; discard clams or mussels that remain closed.
Finish with the listed herbs, citrus or dairy and serve hot.
recipes.sides: Serve hot with jasmine rice.
recipes.substitutions: Use mushrooms and soy sauce for a vegetarian broth.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked leftovers in a covered shallow container within 2 hours and use within 3 days; reheat once until steaming. Do not save raw marinade that touched meat or seafood.
recipes.safety: Keep raw seafood chilled and separate from ready-to-eat foods. Cook fish to 63 C; shrimp, scallops, crab and lobster should be firm and opaque. Discard clams and mussels that do not open. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.name: Massaman fish curry
recipes.description: Massaman fish curry is a Southern Thailand-style dish featuring firm fish, simmered in a spiced sauce, with 300 ml coconut milk, 2 tbsp massaman curry paste. Tip: Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer after adding seafood.
instructions: Cook the onion and curry paste in the listed oil over medium heat until fragrant. Stir in the measured coconut milk, stock or water.
Add vegetables and simmer until nearly tender. Taste the sauce and balance with the listed acid or seasoning.
Add fish or prawns for the final 5-10 minutes, simmering gently until fish reaches 63 C and prawns are firm and opaque.
Serve hot with the listed rice or bread. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.
recipes.sides: Serve with jasmine rice and lime.
recipes.substitutions: Use chickpeas and vegetables instead of fish.

recipes.description: Shorshe ilish mustard hilsa is a Bengal-style dish featuring hilsa steaks, steamed with aromatics, with 2 tbsp mustard paste, 1 green chilli. Tip: Arrange pieces in one layer and keep the steamer covered.
instructions: Prepare the seafood and aromatics. Bring 3-5 cm water to a steady simmer in a covered steamer or pot with a rack.
Arrange seafood in a single layer in a heatproof dish; add the listed ginger, herbs, sauce or liquid and cover.
Steam until fish reaches 63 C and flakes, or shrimp/scallops turn opaque; mussels and clams should open. Discard shells that stay closed.

instructions: Soften the onion and aromatics in the listed oil. Stir in the rice and spices until each grain is coated.

Nestle fish and shellfish into the rice for the final cooking period; fish should reach 63 C and shellfish should open. Discard unopened shells.

instructions: Prepare the seafood and measure the seasonings. If the recipe includes a coating, combine it in a shallow dish and coat evenly.

Turn carefully and cook seafood to 63 C; shellfish flesh should be opaque. Drain fried pieces on a rack or paper.
Finish with the listed citrus or herbs and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Escovitch fish
recipes.description: Escovitch fish is a Coastal Jamaica-style dish featuring whole snapper, about 700 g each, lightly coated and fried until crisp, with 1 carrot, 1 red pepper. Tip: Fry in small batches so the oil temperature does not drop.
instructions: Pat the seafood dry and prepare the flour or crumb coating. Heat oil in a heavy pan to 175 C, using a thermometer and leaving plenty of headroom.
Fry in small batches until crisp and golden, turning once. Keep uncooked batches chilled while the oil heats.
Check thick pieces reach 63 C; drain on a rack and let the oil return to temperature between batches.
Serve hot with the listed sauce and lemon. Keep water away from hot oil.
recipes.sides: Top the fish with the hot pickled vegetables; serve with festival bread.
